The mechanism prediction held, and more: at 0 thoughts this model solves 329 (347, 319, 321) against 701's 479 (466, 476, 496), so the 8-vs-0 gap is 219 theorems here against 52 for 701; per-sample eval accuracy at 0 thoughts is 7-9% against 701's 20-23%, while at 8 thoughts both are 30-31%. | 703-fable | Chained thought groups: level n is ceil(n/4) sequential passes of up to 4 thoughts, so 8 thoughts is two passes deep | claude-fable-5-1 | architecture, thoughts | 0.35 | 5400/300/1800 | 116 | 448 | 253 | 751 | discard | 0.8995 | 0.0800 | 415 734 | 2712 | Discard: 448 (425, 427, 493) against 702's 548, with two RL rounds instead of three. The pretraining was not the cost: 1,286-1,335 steps against 702's 1,530-1,651, yet round-1 sample accuracy at 8 thoughts was 8.3/1.9/14.1% against 702's 4.5% mean, and pretraining val loss ordered 8 < 2 < 0 on two seeds (0.0757/0.0760/0.0781 and 0.0778/0.0789/0.0822), which 701 and 702 never showed. The fine-tune was: at 8 thoughts every line is two passes, so the 600-step fine-tune took about 480 s against 702's 195-250 s, each round ran 660-730 s, and the third round no longer fit (751 RL targets after two rounds against 702's 778 after two and 956 after three). Thoughts still matter after RL: 253 at 0 thoughts, a gap of 195 (702: 219); per-sample eval accuracy 20-25% at 8 against 6-7% at 0 (702: 30-31% and 7-9%). Whether two passes beat one is unresolved: the run never sampled at 2 or 4, and the eval only sees 8 and 0. A follow-up should keep three rounds (FT_STEPS 300, or fine-tune at a one-pass level) and sample once at 2, 4 and 8. |
| 704-fable | Pause-slot thoughts: a thought's input is a learned slot vector, not the trigger's output, so a training step is one causal pass | claude-fable-5-1 | thoughts, architecture, systems, simplification | 0.55 | 5400/300/1800 | 122 | 676 | 482 | 1184 | keep | 0.953 | 0.0843 | 568 942 1086 1128 1161 1178 1191 | 3407 | Keep: 676 (682, 680, 667) against 702's 548 (535, 562, 546), up 105-145 on every seed; the first attempt's two surviving seeds scored 640 and 684 (its seed-1 pod had no working CUDA device, pretrained on CPU for 8 steps and timed out, so the whole experiment was re-run under the same registration; the first attempt is archived in artifacts/autoresearch_thoughts/previous_attempts). But the thoughts are not what scored. metric_diag at 0 thoughts is 670 and 656 on seeds 0 and 1, within 12-24 of the 8-thought score, and pretraining val loss is flat in the thought count on every seed (8 against 0 within 0.001). Seed 2's 121 at 0 thoughts is the no-thought path going out of distribution under RL that trains at 8 only (702's 329 came by the same route), not computation in the slots, since the identical recipe left seeds 0 and 1 level. So the spike's finding holds per line too: pause slots go unused, and the fed-back trigger state of 701-703 was what made 8 thoughts beat 0 there. The gain is speed. Single-pass training gave 3,398-3,784 pretraining steps (702: 1,530-1,651) and fine-tunes of 76-118 s instead of 195-254 s, so RL ran 6-7 rounds instead of 3 (RL targets 1,184 against 956) with 1,564-1,729 of 1,800 s charged. Two predictions failed: the pretraining val loss did not fall (0.0843-0.0869 against 702's 0.0817-0.0844 at 2.2x the steps, though held-out greedy accuracy rose to 0.953-0.963 from 0.899-0.920), so per step the pause model learns less than the feedback model; and the thoughts' contribution did not survive without feedback. Round-1 sample accuracy at 8 thoughts varied 5.4-18.9% across seeds (first attempt 2.6-5.2%), so pretrained-model variance stays large. Next: put the feedback back on top of this single-pass trunk at a cost below one pass per line (thought inputs from a lower block's state at the trigger, or one extra pass over the expanded sequence), and read whether 8 beats 0 in the pretraining val loss, the cheap place to see it. |
| 705-fable | Plain-state feedback: a thought's input is the no-thought network's final state at the trigger, one detached forward, so training stays one pass | claude-fable-5-1 | thoughts, architecture | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 101 | 5 | 3 | 26 | crash | 0.0 | 0.5629 | 0 | 2875 | Crash, not the idea's fault: metric 5 (0, 0, 16) because pretraining ran without gradients to the block matrices. run() computes the plain network's state under torch.no_grad first in the autocast region; autocast caches the bf16 casts of the weights that pass makes, those casts carry no grad_fn, and the expanded pass with gradients reused them, so on every batch with thoughts qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 got no gradient (and Muon's CUDA graph, captured on step 1, kept replaying stale momentum). Reproduced under the pod's torch 2.9.1 on CPU: a toy Linear after such a pass raises 'does not require grad', and the real model's block matrices get zero gradient; torch 2.14 no longer caches casts made without grad, which is why the local check_model/CPU tests passed. Pretraining val loss 0.56-0.57 at 0 thoughts against 704's 0.085, held-out greedy 0.000, feedback_gain 0.019, train loss flat near 0.55-0.60 from step 500; 0 proofs in RL on seeds 0 and 1, seed 2 found 79 targets in 5 rounds and scored 16. The fix is one line after the no_grad pass, torch.clear_autocast_cache(): with it the block matrices get gradients under 2.9.1 and bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 gives val loss 0.0868 at 469 steps (704's bench: 0.0919 at 552), 10.4 steps/s steady against 704's 12.2 (the broken file's 12.0 was fast because the backward skipped the weight gradients), 16.8 GB peak, 95 samples/s at 8 thoughts with the Lean gate. A committed registration is immutable, so run_idea.py refused the fixed file under 705; the next session should register 706 as this patch plus that line. The fixed file, its diff and its registration text (same hypothesis, corrected speed numbers) are in artifacts/autoresearch_thoughts/705-fable_plain-state-feedback/pretrain_fixed.py, pretrain_fixed.patch and params_fixed.json (local, gitignored). One more correction for 706: the gain-1 bench (loss 0.74 at 543 steps) that motivated the zero gain init had the same bug, so that reading was wrong and the zero init is untested; 702's unit gain may be the better start. |
| 706-fable | Sibling loop's RL recipe (507): 8 samples per target then 24 retries on the failures, fine-tune over 76,800 records in token-budget batches, all at 8 thoughts | claude-fable-5-1 | rl, sampling, systems | 0.85 | 5400/300/1800 | 123 | 574 | 565 | 1019 | discard | 0.933 | 0.0850 | 162 223 752 859 1034 1076 1124 1142 1160 1176 1186 1194 1199 1212 1214 1218 1225 1226 1231 1236 1238 1239 | 3447 | Discard: 574 (726, 699, 297) against 704's 676 (682, 680, 667). The recipe ran as designed: 11/9/7 RL rounds (704: 7/6/6), fine-tunes of 577-719 AdamW steps in token-budget batches taking 47-60 s against 704's 76-118 s, rounds of 140-230 s of RL clock against 704's 230-250, and 1,239/1,193/624 RL targets by the end (704: 1,191/1,189/1,173). It did not transfer 590's 792: the two seeds that took off scored 726 and 699 with 48 and 4 more RL targets than 704's, so on a model past take-off the extra rounds bought +20 to +45, and the third seed never took off and scored 297. Expert iteration here has a take-off: first-pass acceptance sits at 0.25-0.40 for several rounds, then jumps to 0.6-0.7 in one round (seed 1: 0.396 at round 7 and 0.680 at round 8, 719 to 1,128 targets; seed 0 took off at round 2, 0.053 to 0.336 to 0.598; 704's seed 2 did the same at round 5, 0.357 to 0.653). Seed 2 ran 7 rounds at 0.028, 0.174, 0.253, 0.303, 0.337, 0.365, 0.382 and ended at 624 targets. Below take-off the retries are the wrong use of the budget: retrying 880-1,400 failed targets 24 times cost 100-170 s of each 210-290 s round and cracked 5-44 targets a round (acceptance 0.03-0.4%), where the first pass plus fine-tune alone (about 110 s) would have fit about 15 rounds; past take-off they cost 50-80 s and cracked 3-22 (acceptance up to 1.3%). New distinct proofs per first pass on the stuck seeds were 72-110 against 189-492 per 32-sample round for 704's seed 2 at the same acceptance, so a stuck seed's fine-tune mix grows by under 100 proofs a round; whether the diversity of proofs on already-solved targets is what triggers take-off is the open question, and the next rl() experiment should test it (a first pass of 16-32, no retries) rather than port more of the sibling's recipe. All three pretrained models were the weak kind: round-1 acceptance 5.3/4.8/2.8% at 8 thoughts (704's run: 18.9/11.4/5.4%; its first attempt 2.6-5.2%; same code and seeds), 3,418-3,449 steps, val 0.085-0.089, held-out greedy 0.933-0.957 (704: 0.953-0.963), so part of the gap to 704 is the pretraining lottery, which under this take-off dynamic dominates a 3-seed mean. Thoughts: metric_diag 707/686/302 is within 13-19 of metric on every seed, so the no-thought path stayed in distribution through 9-11 rounds of fine-tuning at 8 thoughts (704's seed 2 drifted to 121) and the slots compute nothing, as in 704. So most of the 115 points between 590 and 704 are not in this rl() recipe; the remaining suspects are the pretraining (198's 5,000+ steps against 3,400 here with slots, probe and MTP) and the fine-tune at 8 thoughts. |
| 707-fable | Plain-state feedback: a thought's input is the no-thought network's final state at the trigger, one detached forward, so training stays one pass (705's idea with its autocast fix) | claude-fable-5-1 | thoughts, architecture | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 105 | 638 | 589 | 1113 | discard | 0.9365 | 0.0845 | 361 867 1046 1125 | 3266 | Discard: 638 (639, 652, 622) against 704's 676 (682, 680, 667), below on every seed. The feedback is not what the model learned to use. Pretraining val loss at 8 thoughts minus at 0: -0.0014, +0.0008, -0.0013 (predicted at least -0.002 on every seed; 704: -0.0010, -0.0002, +0.0000), so thoughts fed the plain network's state at the trigger reduce the loss no more than 704's pause slots; the prediction failed on every seed, and a seed went the wrong way. The gain opened from 0 to a mean \|weight\| of 0.042/0.041/0.044 after pretraining (predicted above 0.2) and RL left it there (0.043/0.042/0.045). Scale: a LayerNorm output has unit variance per element, so at 0.04 the fed-back vector has the per-element scale of a token embedding at initialization (std 0.02), not nothing; whether it is small against the trained embeddings and slot vectors is unmeasured (checkpoints are not pulled). Either way the loss did not pull it further: with the draft detached, the thoughts find nothing in the model's own reading of the context that they could not already reach through attention. 701-703's used thoughts had gradient through the fed-back state, and that joint training remains the surviving explanation. The score is the cost of a second network with no benefit. Pretraining got 2,937-2,974 steps (704: 3,398-3,784) at the same end val loss at 8 thoughts (0.0832-0.0858 against 704's 0.0843-0.0869), so per step the feedback model learns a little more, as the bench said. In RL every token runs through both networks: sampling 119-153 samples/s (704: 181-207), rounds of 350-493 s (704: 267-329), so 4 rounds fit instead of 6-7, 1,097-1,125 RL targets (704: 1,173-1,191), 1,511-1,644 s charged, total 2,932-3,266 s. metric_diag 571/625/572, 27-68 below metric (per-sample eval accuracy 0.40-0.41 at 8 thoughts against 0.30-0.36 at 0; 704: 0.43-0.45 at 8), where 704's seeds 0 and 1 sat 12-24 below: with the val loss flat in n this is the no-thought path drifting under the 8-only fine-tune (perhaps a little further here because at 8 the model also sees the 0.04-scaled draft), not computation in the thoughts. Round-1 acceptance 4.2/6.0/6.8% at 8 thoughts, held-out greedy 0.936-0.958: the weak kind of pretrained model again (704: 18.9/11.4/5.4; 706: 5.3/4.8/2.8). Next: the zero gain init may be a trap (the thoughts' downstream weights train on the slots, a random-direction draft gets a small gradient on the gain, and nothing forces it open); gain 1 from the start, 701-703's init, is untested here and costs one run. The other reading, that the gradient through the fed-back state is what makes thoughts matter, needs a second backward (702's 0.45x speed) and the speed problem solved first. |
